text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on April 21 in history:
753 BC - According to the historian Varro, Romulus founded Rome on this day.
1109 - Saint Anselm of Canterbury, one of the founders of medieval scholasticism, died.
1509 - King Henry VII of England died. His accession to the throne in 1485 ended the Wars of the Roses between the houses of Lancaster and York.
1634 - Jan van Riebeeck, Dutch naval surgeon, born; best known as the founder of Cape Town (1652), which helped open South Africa for whites.
1699 - Jean Racine, one of the greatest French poets and playwrights, died.
1816 - Charlotte Bronte, eldest of the three literary sisters, born. Her publisher rejected her first novel, "The Professor", but she went on to write her masterpiece "Jane Eyre".
1836 - The Mexicans were defeated by the Texans at the battle of San Jacinto, thus ensuring Texan independence.

1910 - American novelist Mark Twain (Samuel Langhorne Clemens) died. His two masterpieces, "The Adventures of Tom Sawyer" and "The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn", are drawn from his own boyhood experiences.
1918 - Manfred von Richthofen, Germany's top aviator in World War One, was killed in action. Known as the Red Baron, he shot down 80 enemy aircraft.
1926 - Elizabeth II, Queen of the United Kingdom since 1952, born.
1945 - The last of the German troops motored out of Bologna, Italy; on the same day Russian troops reached the suburbs of Berlin.
1946 - John Maynard Keynes, English economist and journalist, died; best known for his theory on the causes of prolonged unemployment.

1952 - Sir Stafford Cripps, British statesman and chancellor of the exchequer, died. As chancellor, his policy of austerity caught the public imagination and led the trade unions to impose a voluntary wage freeze.
1959 - English ballerina Dame Margot Fonteyn was jailed for a day in Panama while the police looked for her Panamanian husband, accused of plotting a coup.
1960 - Brasilia was inaugurated as the new capital of Brazil.
1961 - A French army revolt led by General Maurice Challe began in Algeria.
1965 - The 114-nation U.N. Disarmament Commission resumed talks in New York after a five-year interval.
1967 - A military coup in Athens established the regime of the "Greek Colonels".
1968 - British Conservative politician Enoch Powell made his "rivers of blood" warning of the dangers of immigration, where he called for a stiffening of policy.
1968 - Canadian Prime Minister Lester Pearson resigned and was succeeded by Pierre Trudeau.
1971 - Francois "Papa Doc" Duvalier, president of Haiti since 1957, died. He ran the country as a tyrannical dictatorship and created a gangster militia known as the Tonton Macoute.
1975 - South Vietnamese President Nguyen Van Thieu resigned after 10 years in office.
1985 - Tancredo Neves, Brazilian president-elect, died on the eve of his swearing-in.
1990 - Erte (Romain de Tirtoff), prolific Russian-born Art Deco designer, died. He created the 1920s sets for America's Ziegfield Folies and France's Folies Bergeres.
1992 - California carried out its first execution in 25 years, when double murderer Robert Alton Harris was put to death in the gas chamber.
1994 - A Belfast court cleared Paul Hill of the 1974 murder of a former British soldier, formally absolving him of IRA guerrilla links for which he was wrongfully jailed for 13 years.
1996 - The centre-left Olive Tree coalition won the Italian general election, the left's first win since World War Two.
